company: Clean TeQ Holdings Limited (ASX: SRL, now Sunrise Energy Metals Limited)
title: Share Trading Policy

tiers.name: Employee
tiers.description: Group employees and any contractor or consultant who is regularly engaged by the Company or has been engaged by the Company for at least two continuous weeks over the past year, other than a Designated Officer.

tiers.name: Designated Officer
tiers.description: A director or person engaged in the management of the Group, whether as an Employee or consultant (ie key management personnel).

tiers.name: Directors (other than the chairperson of the Audit Committee)
tiers.description: Sub-group of Designated Officer distinguished only for clearance: approved by the chairperson of the Audit Committee.

tiers.name: Chairperson of the Audit Committee
tiers.description: Sub-group of Designated Officer distinguished only for clearance: approved by the Managing Director or CEO.

tiers.name: Associates and investment managers
tiers.description: Any associate of, or investment manager acting for, an Employee or Designated Officer; must be informed of, and prohibited from dealing during, any period the Employee or Designated Officer may not deal.

definitions.hedging_definition: transactions ... which operate to limit the economic risk of holding any security in the Company or any vested or unvested entitlements to securities in the Company under any equity based remuneration schemes offered by the Company (or any member of the Group)

windows.end_anchor: the date of release of the Company's quarterly results to ASX

24 hours after the announcement of the Company's full year results to ASX
24 hours after the Company's annual general meeting

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Managing Director or CEO may declare, in writing to Employees and Directors, an alternative Blackout Period or Executive Trading Window time. The Policy does not state whether such a declaration, or a refusal of clearance, must be kept confidential.

rules.detail: Company Securities is expressly defined to include any derivative the value of which is determined by a Company security. A plain (non-risk-limiting) derivative dealing by an Employee needs no clearance, only compliance with the insider trading and Blackout Period rules; a risk-limiting derivative such as a collar is separately and absolutely banned under clause 14.
rules.evidence: any derivative or associated instruments the value of which is determined (in whole or in part) by any security listed in paragraph (a), (b) or (c)

rules.detail: Derivatives are expressly within Company Securities. A Designated Officer may deal in an Executive Trading Window if they immediately notify the Approving Officer, or outside a window (but not in a Blackout Period) only with prior written clearance under paragraph 9.
rules.evidence: a Designated Officer may only deal in Company Securities: (a) during the Executive Trading Windows, so long as he or she immediately notifies the Approving Officer of the dealing; or (b) outside the Executive Trading Windows ... if he or she has complied with paragraph 9

rules.detail: Blanket, unconditional ban on hedging arrangements (and any other risk-limiting transaction) in Company Securities or derivatives thereof, covering both securities already held and vested or unvested equity-remuneration entitlements, for all Employees and Designated Officers. No clearance or exemption route is provided for this ban.
rules.evidence: Employees and Designated Officers are not permitted to enter into transactions (includes, but is not limited to, hedging arrangements, margin loans and / or share lending arrangements) in Company Securities (or any derivative thereof) which operate to limit the economic risk of holding any security in the Company or any vested or unvested entitlements to securities in the Company under any equity based remuneration schemes offered by the Company (or any member of the Group).

rules.detail: Monetisation (e.g. a prepaid forward) is not separately named, but it is a transaction that operates to limit the economic risk of holding Company Securities and so falls within clause 14's open-ended ('includes, but is not limited to') prohibition.
rules.evidence: transactions ... which operate to limit the economic risk of holding any security in the Company

rules.detail: Short selling (borrowing and selling to profit from a price fall) is not named. Clause 13's 'speculative dealing' ban addresses considerations of a short-term nature, not the borrow-and-sell technique specifically.
Share lending arrangements are expressly named as a prohibited risk-limiting transaction, applying to all Employees and Designated Officers.
rules.evidence: transactions (includes, but is not limited to, hedging arrangements, margin loans and / or share lending arrangements)

rules.detail: A CFD referencing Company Securities is a derivative within the Company Securities definition. A non-risk-limiting CFD dealing by an Employee needs no clearance; a risk-limiting CFD position is banned under clause 14.
rules.evidence: any derivative or associated instruments the value of which is determined (in whole or in part) by any security listed in paragraph (a), (b) or (c)

rules.detail: CFDs are derivatives within Company Securities and so subject to the same window-notification or out-of-window clearance regime as any other Dealing by a Designated Officer.
rules.evidence: a Designated Officer may only deal in Company Securities: (a) during the Executive Trading Windows, so long as he or she immediately notifies the Approving Officer of the dealing; or (b) outside the Executive Trading Windows ... if he or she has complied with paragraph 9

rules.detail: Margin loans in respect of Company Securities are expressly named as a prohibited risk-limiting transaction, applying to all Employees and Designated Officers, over any security or any vested or unvested remuneration entitlement.
rules.evidence: transactions (includes, but is not limited to, hedging arrangements, margin loans and / or share lending arrangements) in Company Securities (or any derivative thereof) which operate to limit the economic risk of holding any security in the Company

rules.detail: Granting a charge or other security interest is not separately named, but margin loans (which are a form of encumbrance) are expressly prohibited and clause 14's list is 'not limited to' the named examples.
rules.evidence: transactions (includes, but is not limited to, hedging arrangements, margin loans and / or share lending arrangements) in Company Securities

rules.detail: Clause 14's ban is not limited to margin loans by name ('includes, but is not limited to'); a bank loan secured against the collared shares operates in substance like the named margin loan example and is caught, with no clearance or exemption route available.
rules.evidence: transactions (includes, but is not limited to, hedging arrangements, margin loans and / or share lending arrangements) in Company Securities (or any derivative thereof) which operate to limit the economic risk of holding any security in the Company

rules.detail: Ban on dealing in Company Securities on considerations of a short-term nature, applying to all Employees and Designated Officers. No period is quantified and no clearance route is referenced for this ban.
rules.evidence: An Employee or Designated Officer may not deal in Company Securities on considerations of a short term nature.

exceptions.evidence: other than acquiring securities pursuant to the Group Employee Incentive Plan
A decision to join, or subscribe for Company Securities under, any dividend reinvestment plan or other corporate action open to all shareholders is not dealing in Company Securities.

The Approving Officer may give clearance for an Employee or Designated Officer to Deal in Company Securities in exceptional circumstances where the Designated Officer would otherwise not be able to do so under this policy. For example, if the Designated Officer has a pressing financial commitment that cannot otherwise be satisfied.

exemption_authority: The Approving Officer may give clearance to Deal in exceptional circumstances (e.g. a pressing financial commitment that cannot otherwise be satisfied) where the person would otherwise not be able to deal, but may not give clearance at all if there is inside information about the Company or any other reason to believe the dealing would breach the Policy; the Approving Officer decides whether circumstances are exceptional. This discretion only relieves the Blackout Period/Executive Trading Window timing restrictions -- it does not extend to, and cannot waive, the absolute clause 14 ban on hedging, margin loans and share lending.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees and Designated Officers are not permitted to enter into transactions (includes, but is not limited to, hedging arrangements, margin loans and / or share lending arrangements) in Company Securities (or any derivative thereof) which operate to limit the economic risk of holding any security in the Company or any vested or unvested entitlements to securities in the Company under any equity based remuneration schemes offered by the Company (or any member of the Group).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This single clause bans both legs of a funded collar outright -- the hedge (put and call) and any margin loan or other risk-limiting financing -- for all Employees and Designated Officers, across vested and unvested holdings, with no clearance or exemption route referenced anywhere in the Policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: transactions (includes, but is not limited to, hedging arrangements, margin loans and / or share lending arrangements)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The 'not limited to' wording means a bespoke secured loan or novel collar structure cannot be argued to fall outside the ban merely because it is not called a margin loan or hedge by name.

bespoke_clauses.clause: which operate to limit the economic risk of holding any security in the Company or any vested or unvested entitlements to securities in the Company under any equity based remuneration schemes offered by the Company
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The prohibition is not confined to incentive-plan securities -- it extends to 'any security in the Company', so open-market purchased shares held by a director or executive are equally covered.

bespoke_clauses.clause: I acknowledge that this approval to trade is value for only fourteen (14) days from the date indicated below, unless otherwise revoked earlier by notice in writing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even for the narrow set of dealings not caught by clause 14 (e.g. an outright sale of vested shares outside a window), a Designated Officer's clearance to trade lapses after 14 days.

bespoke_clauses.clause: [The Policy does not state that a refusal of clearance must be kept confidential, nor that the Approving Officer may impose conditions on a clearance.]
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike most peer policies, there is no express confidentiality protection around a refused clearance request and no explicit power to attach conditions; clearance here is effectively binary.

summary: A funded collar is not available under this Policy for any Employee or Designated Officer, at any vesting stage: clause 14 imposes a blanket, unconditional ban on entering into transactions -- expressly including hedging arrangements, margin loans and share lending arrangements, and by its 'includes, but is not limited to' wording likely any other risk-limiting or secured financing arrangement -- that operate to limit the economic risk of holding any Company security or any vested or unvested equity-remuneration entitlement. No clearance, exemption or exceptional-circumstances route in the Policy reaches this prohibition; the exceptional-circumstances discretion in clause 10 only relieves the Blackout Period and Executive Trading Window timing restrictions on ordinary dealing, not the clause 14 ban. Outside of a collar structure, an outright sale or purchase of vested shares by a Designated Officer requires prior written clearance from the Approving Officer (the Managing Director/CEO, or the chairperson of the Audit Committee for other directors), valid for only 14 days, and is barred altogether during quarterly Blackout Periods and while in possession of inside information; ordinary Employees face no clearance requirement but the same Blackout Period and insider trading restrictions apply. Because margin loans and share lending are outright prohibitions rather than merely regulated activities, the Policy contains no secured-lender enforcement carve-out and no financing disclosure regime. In short, the bank's funded collar cannot be offered to directors or executives of this company under the current Policy.
